CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

- context7-mcp: This skill should be used when the user asks about libraries, frameworks, API references, or needs code examples. Activates for setup questions, code generation involving libraries, or mentions of specific frameworks like React, Vue, Next.js, Prisma, Supabase, etc.
- paperclip: Interact with the Paperclip control plane API to manage tasks, coordinate with other agents, and follow company governance. Use when you need to check assignments, update task status, delegate work, post comments, set up or manage routines (recurring scheduled tasks), or call any Paperclip API endpoint. Do NOT use for the actual domain work itself (writing code, research, etc.) — only for Paperclip coordination.
- paperclip-converting-plans-to-tasks: The Paperclip way of converting a plan into executable tasks. Use whenever you are asked to plan, scope, or break down work inside a Paperclip company. Industry-agnostic guidance on how to translate a plan into assigned issues with the right specialty, dependencies, and parallelization so Paperclip's executor can pick up the work — it does not prescribe a plan format. Pair with the `paperclip` skill, which covers the mechanics of writing the plan document and reassigning the issue.
- paperclip-create-agent: Create new agents in Paperclip with governance-aware hiring. Use when you need to inspect adapter configuration options, compare existing agent configs, draft a new agent prompt/config, and submit a hire request.
- paperclip-dev: Develop and operate a local Paperclip instance — start and stop servers, pull updates from master, run builds and tests, manage worktrees, back up databases, and diagnose problems. Use whenever you need to work on the Paperclip codebase itself or keep a running instance healthy.
- para-memory-files: File-based memory system using Tiago Forte's PARA method. Use this skill whenever you need to store, retrieve, update, or organize knowledge across sessions. Covers three memory layers: (1) Knowledge graph in PARA folders with atomic YAML facts, (2) Daily notes as raw timeline, (3) Tacit knowledge about user patterns. Also handles planning files, memory decay, weekly synthesis, and recall via qmd. Trigger on any memory operation: saving facts, writing daily notes, creating entities, running weekly synthesis, recalling past context, or managing plans.
- subagents: Orcistrator Skill
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

# NEONSTRIKE — ray-traced arena FPS

Fast-paced CS-style shooter where the entire frame is ray traced in a WebGL2
fragment shader. No triangles are rasterized: every pixel casts a primary ray
against the analytic scene (level AABBs + bot spheres), then shadow rays,
ambient-occlusion rays, and up to 3 reflection bounces.

## Run

Static — no build, no server logic. Serve `app/public/` over HTTP
(ES modules forbid `file://`):

```bash
npx serve app/public        # or open via the AI Archives hub
```

Launched from the hub at `/archives/neonstrike/app/public/index.html`.

## Game

- **Map "VECTOR"**: three-lane arena (mid + long A + long B), two sites,
  crates, neon strips that are real emissive light sources.
- **Rounds**: buy phase → live → end; win by eliminating all bots, lose on
  death or timeout; first to 8 rounds takes the match.
- **Economy**: $800 start, +$300/kill, +$3250 win, +$1400 loss.
  Pistols, SMG, shotgun, rifle, scoped sniper, kevlar.
- **Bots**: waypoint-graph patrol, distance + view-cone + ray-traced LOS
  spotting, reaction delay, strafing return fire. 4 difficulty tiers.
- **Settings** (Esc): 37 options across graphics (resolution scale, RT
  bounces, shadow mode/samples, AO, fog, frame cap…), audio, controls,
  crosshair (style/size/gap/color/dynamic), game (bot count, difficulty,
  radar, damage numbers…). Quality presets potato→ultra. Persisted to
  localStorage.

Everything is generated at runtime: textures are procedural GLSL
(triplanar brick/planks/brushed metal/hazard), all 21 SFX are synthesized
Float32Array DSP (verifiable headlessly), the ambient loop included.

## Playtest

`test/playtest.mjs` runs the real game in headless Chrome (SwiftShader
WebGL2) and verifies:

1. boot with zero JS errors
2. menu + 5 in-game vantage screenshots (pixel variance, not-black, sky≠floor)
3. every procedural material renders a distinct swatch
4. every SFX buffer has sane duration/peak/RMS
5. gameplay: hitscan damage, ammo, bot navigation, bots engaging the player,
   round win on elimination, money payouts, buy-phase purchase flow
6. settings: bounces visibly change pixels, resolution scale resizes the RT
   target, persistence
7. perf snapshot per quality preset (software-rendering floor)

```bash
cd test && npm install && npm run playtest
```

Latest result: **60/60 checks passed** — see `playtest/report.md` and
screenshots in `playtest/`.

content.text:
Done — all upgrades shipped, **78/78 playtest checks passing** (including a real two-client networked match).

**Multiplayer with room codes.** New Node WebSocket server (`app/server/index.js`) + client netcode (`net.js`): create a room from the MULTIPLAYER menu, share the 4-letter code (unambiguous alphabet, no 0/O/1/I), up to 8 players in free-for-all deathmatch to 15 kills. Server is authoritative for damage, kills, scores, and respawns; positions sync at 15 Hz with interpolated remote players, TAB scoreboard, respawn overlay, room banner. The playtest spins up two actual browser clients: ALICE creates room, BOB joins by code, they see and render each other, ALICE shoots BOB (server applies damage), kill credits the scoreboard, BOB respawns at 100 hp.

**Map diversity.** Three maps with genuinely different layouts and moods, selectable on the menu: VECTOR (original neon night arena), FOUNDRY (ember-orange furnace hall with raised central platform and ring corridor), CANOPY (violet-dusk rooftops with bridges and a lower street level). The renderer now takes per-map themes — sky, fog, haze, and neon palette are all uniform-driven. Screenshot diff confirms the maps are 94–96% pixel-distinct, and bots navigate all three (4/4 moved on each).

**Characters.** The old two-sphere blobs are now five-sphere humanoid rigs — head, glowing visor, torso, hips, gun hand — with per-bot warm tints and per-player hash-assigned colors, ray traced like everything else. Verified in close-up and multiplayer screenshots.

**Bug fixes** (from the audit agent + one I found playtesting):
- **Netcode lived in the render loop** — browsers pause `requestAnimationFrame` in background tabs, so an alt-tabbed player would freeze for everyone. Moved sync to a 50 ms timer. This is what made the playtest's "both clients see each other" check fail initially.
- Hub spawned every archived game on port 3001 (collision once neonstrike got a server) — ports are now per-entry (`rblx`:3001, `neonstrike`:3002), verified live.
- Settings listener leak on every settings-open; presets not notifying listeners; float garbage in slider readouts.
- Escape now works on settings/lobby/matchend screens; fire/scope state cleared on pointer-lock loss (no stuck auto-fire after pause).
- Killfeed decay was hardcoded to 60 fps; buy menu now grays out owned/unaffordable items and its hint matches the actual buy window; HUD updates during buy phase; buy menu no longer overflows small windows.

Archive entry and README updated; your running hub is already serving the new build at `http://localhost:3002`.

# NEONSTRIKE weapon factory. Builds all 7 weapons as real meshes and renders
# them with Cycles (GPU-style path tracing on CPU) to transparent PNGs:
#   <id>_vm.png   1024x640  side view for the in-game viewmodel
#   <id>_card.png 512x320   3/4 hero shot for the buy menu
# Run:  blender -b -P weapons.py -- <out_dir>
import bpy
import math
import sys

OUT = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1] if '--' in sys.argv else '/tmp/weapons'

NEON = (0.24, 1.0, 0.78, 1.0)        # game accent #3dffc8
DARK = (0.013, 0.015, 0.022, 1.0)    # receiver body
MID = (0.05, 0.055, 0.07, 1.0)       # furniture
STEEL = (0.35, 0.38, 0.42, 1.0)
WOODY = (0.18, 0.10, 0.045, 1.0)

def reset():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    sc.cycles.samples = 96
    sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
    sc.render.film_transparent = True
    sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
    sc.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
    return sc

def mat(name, base, rough=0.45, metal=0.0, emit=None, emit_str=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = base
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    if emit is not None:
        bsdf.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = emit
        bsdf.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = emit_str
    return m

def box(name, sx, sy, sz, x=0, y=0, z=0, m=None, bevel=0.012):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(x, y, z))
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = (sx, sy, sz)
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    if bevel > 0:
        mod = o.modifiers.new('bv', 'BEVEL')
        mod.width = bevel
        mod.segments = 2
    if m: o.data.materials.append(m)
    return o

def cyl(name, r, depth, x=0, y=0, z=0, rot=(0, math.pi / 2, 0), m=None, verts=24):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=r, depth=depth, location=(x, y, z), rotation=rot, vertices=verts)
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    if m: o.data.materials.append(m)
    return o

# ---------------- weapon builders ----------------
# All built lying along +X (muzzle at +X), sights up (+Z). Unit ~ meters.

def grip_and_trigger(M, x_grip, scale=1.0):
    g = box('grip', 0.05 * scale, 0.042, 0.16 * scale, x_grip, 0, -0.085 * scale, M['mid'], 0.01)
    g.rotation_euler[1] = -0.32
    box('guard', 0.085 * scale, 0.012, 0.012, x_grip + 0.055, 0, -0.052 * scale, M['mid'], 0.004)
    cyl('trigger', 0.018, 0.01, x_grip + 0.045, 0, -0.035 * scale, (math.pi / 2, 0, 0), M['steel'], 8)

def mats():
    return {
        'dark': mat('dark', DARK, 0.32, 0.6),
        'mid': mat('mid', MID, 0.5, 0.25),
        'steel': mat('steel', STEEL, 0.22, 1.0),
        'neon': mat('neon', (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1), 0.4, 0.0, NEON, 14.0),
        'glass': mat('glass', (0.06, 0.2, 0.16, 1), 0.05, 0.0, (0.1, 0.6, 0.45, 1), 2.0),
        'wood': mat('wood', WOODY, 0.6, 0.0),
    }

def w_pistol(M):
    box('slide', 0.30, 0.046, 0.052, 0.02, 0, 0.045, M['dark'])
    box('frame', 0.24, 0.044, 0.03, -0.01, 0, 0.005, M['mid'])
    cyl('muzzle', 0.014, 0.04, 0.17, 0, 0.045, m=M['steel'])
    box('sight_f', 0.012, 0.01, 0.014, 0.15, 0, 0.078, M['dark'], 0.002)
    box('sight_r', 0.022, 0.024, 0.012, -0.11, 0, 0.077, M['dark'], 0.002)
    box('stripe', 0.27, 0.0485, 0.006, 0.01, 0, 0.026, M['neon'], 0.001)
    grip_and_trigger(M, -0.09, 0.9)
    # slide serrations
    for i in range(5):
        box(f'ser{i}', 0.006, 0.05, 0.04, -0.10 + i * 0.018, 0, 0.05, M['mid'], 0.001)

    box('slide', 0.36, 0.056, 0.07, 0.03, 0, 0.05, M['steel'])

    grip_and_trigger(M, -0.07)
    box('sight', 0.05, 0.02, 0.035, 0.1, 0, 0.1, M['dark'], 0.004)

    cyl('barrel', 0.019, 0.6, 0.18, 0, 0.065, m=M['dark'])

    box('stripe', 0.2, 0.054, 0.007, -0.16, 0, 0.012, M['neon'], 0.001)

def w_rifle(M):
    box('receiver', 0.34, 0.05, 0.08, -0.05, 0, 0.035, M['dark'])
    box('handguard', 0.3, 0.046, 0.06, 0.21, 0, 0.04, M['mid'], 0.008)
    for i in range(6):
        cyl(f'vent{i}', 0.006, 0.05, 0.12 + i * 0.045, 0, 0.073, (math.pi / 2, 0, 0), M['dark'], 8)
    cyl('barrel', 0.013, 0.16, 0.43, 0, 0.045, m=M['steel'])
    box('brake', 0.05, 0.03, 0.034, 0.52, 0, 0.045, M['dark'], 0.005)

    box('rail', 0.3, 0.024, 0.012, -0.0, 0, 0.082, M['mid'], 0.003)
    box('sight_f', 0.014, 0.014, 0.03, 0.35, 0, 0.095, M['dark'], 0.002)

def reset():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    sc.cycles.samples = 96
    sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
    sc.render.film_transparent = True
    sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
    sc.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
    return sc

def mat(name, base, rough=0.45, metal=0.0, emit=None, emit_str=0.0):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = base
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    bsdf.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    if emit is not None:
        bsdf.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = emit
        bsdf.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = emit_str
    return m

def box(name, sx, sy, sz, x=0, y=0, z=0, m=None, bevel=0.012):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(x, y, z))
    o = bpy.context.object
    o.name = name
    o.scale = (sx, sy, sz)
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
    if bevel > 0:
        mod = o.modifiers.new('bv', 'BEVEL')
        mod.width = bevel
        mod.segments = 2
    if m: o.data.materials.append(m)
    return o

import bpy

import os
import sys

# material id -> (base color, rough, metal) matching the in-game shader

    0: ((0.10, 0.105, 0.125, 1), 0.7, 0.0),   # floor
    1: ((0.40, 0.16, 0.12, 1), 0.85, 0.0),    # brick
    2: ((0.42, 0.28, 0.14, 1), 0.8, 0.0),     # crate
    3: ((0.45, 0.49, 0.55, 1), 0.3, 1.0),     # metal
    6: ((0.10, 0.11, 0.14, 1), 0.45, 0.7),    # dark metal
    7: ((0.52, 0.50, 0.45, 1), 0.9, 0.0),     # plaster
    10: ((0.72, 0.35, 0.05, 1), 0.75, 0.0),   # hazard
}

def mat_basic(name, color, rough, metal):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = color
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def mat_neon(name, rgb):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    mx = max(rgb) or 1
    col = (rgb[0] / mx, rgb[1] / mx, rgb[2] / mx, 1)
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0, 0, 0, 1)
    b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = col
    b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = 22.0 * mx
    return m

for map_id, md in DATA.items():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)

    sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    sc.cycles.samples = 128
    sc.cycles.use_denoising = True

# NEONSTRIKE map dioramas. Reads blender/mapdata.json (exported from the real
# maps.js), rebuilds each arena in Blender with theme-matched materials, and
# renders an isometric Cycles hero shot per map for the menu map picker.
# Run:  blender -b -P dioramas.py -- <out_dir>
import bpy
import json
import math
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1] if '--' in sys.argv else '/tmp/maps'
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

DATA = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'mapdata.json')))

# material id -> (base color, rough, metal) matching the in-game shader
MAT_LOOK = {
    0: ((0.10, 0.105, 0.125, 1), 0.7, 0.0),   # floor
    1: ((0.40, 0.16, 0.12, 1), 0.85, 0.0),    # brick
    2: ((0.42, 0.28, 0.14, 1), 0.8, 0.0),     # crate
    3: ((0.45, 0.49, 0.55, 1), 0.3, 1.0),     # metal
    6: ((0.10, 0.11, 0.14, 1), 0.45, 0.7),    # dark metal
    7: ((0.52, 0.50, 0.45, 1), 0.9, 0.0),     # plaster
    10: ((0.72, 0.35, 0.05, 1), 0.75, 0.0),   # hazard
}

def mat_basic(name, color, rough, metal):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = color
    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
    return m

def mat_neon(name, rgb):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
    mx = max(rgb) or 1
    col = (rgb[0] / mx, rgb[1] / mx, rgb[2] / mx, 1)
    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0, 0, 0, 1)
    b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = col
    b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = 22.0 * mx
    return m

for map_id, md in DATA.items():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    sc.cycles.samples = 128
    sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
    sc.render.film_transparent = False
    sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
    sc.view_settings.look = 'High Contrast'

    theme = md['THEME']
    # world: theme sky as a gradient-ish flat color (horizon tone)
    world = bpy.data.worlds.new('w')
    sc.world = world
    world.use_nodes = True
    bg = world.node_tree.nodes['Background']
    sh = theme['skyHorizon']
    bg.inputs['Color'].default_value = (sh[0], sh[1], sh[2], 1)
    bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 0.6

    mats = {k: mat_basic(f'm{k}', *v) for k, v in MAT_LOOK.items()}
    mats[4] = mat_neon('neonA', theme['neonA'])
    mats[5] = mat_neon('neonB', theme['neonB'])

    cx, cz = 0.0, 0.0
    for i, b in enumerate(md['BOXES']):
        x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, mid = b
        w, h, d = x1 - x0, y1 - y0, z1 - z0
        # blender: z up; game: y up -> map (x, z, y)
        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=((x0 + x1) / 2, (z0 + z1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2))
        o = bpy.context.object
        o.scale = (w, d, h)
        bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)
        o.data.materials.append(mats.get(int(mid), mats[7]))

    # theme lights (convert a handful to point lamps)
    for L in md['LIGHTS'][:10]:
        x, y, z, r, g, bch, inten = L
        if inten <= 0: continue
        bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='POINT', location=(x, z, y))
        lamp = bpy.context.object
        lamp.data.color = (r, g, bch)
        lamp.data.energy = inten * 60
        lamp.data.shadow_soft_size = 0.6

    # sun
    sd = md['SUN_DIR']; scol = md['SUN_COLOR']
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='SUN')
    sun = bpy.context.object
    sun.data.color = (scol[0], scol[1], scol[2])
    sun.data.energy = 2.2
    import mathutils
    sun.rotation_euler = mathutils.Vector((-sd[0], -sd[2], -sd[1])).to_track_quat('Z', 'Y').to_euler()

    # isometric-ish camera: high 3/4 from south-east, frame whole arena
    ground = md['BOXES'][0]
    span = max(ground[3] - ground[0], ground[5] - ground[2])
    dist = span * 1.25
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(dist * 0.62, -dist * 0.78, dist * 0.66))
    cam = bpy.context.object
    cam.rotation_euler = mathutils.Vector((-dist * 0.62, dist * 0.78, -dist * 0.62)).to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()
    cam.data.angle = math.radians(35)
    sc.camera = cam

    sc.render.resolution_x = 720
    sc.render.resolution_y = 420
    sc.render.filepath = f'{OUT}/{map_id}.png'
    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
    print(f'rendered diorama {map_id}')

attachment.snippet:
1	# NEONSTRIKE map dioramas. Reads blender/mapdata.json (exported from the real
2	# maps.js), rebuilds each arena in Blender with theme-matched materials, and
3	# renders an isometric Cycles hero shot per map for the menu map picker.
4	# Run:  blender -b -P dioramas.py -- <out_dir>
5	import bpy
6	import json
7	import math
8	import os
9	import sys
10	
11	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
12	OUT = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--') + 1] if '--' in sys.argv else '/tmp/maps'
13	os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
14	
15	DATA = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'mapdata.json')))
16	
17	# material id -> (base color, rough, metal) matching the in-game shader
18	MAT_LOOK = {
19	    0: ((0.10, 0.105, 0.125, 1), 0.7, 0.0),   # floor
20	    1: ((0.40, 0.16, 0.12, 1), 0.85, 0.0),    # brick
21	    2: ((0.42, 0.28, 0.14, 1), 0.8, 0.0),     # crate
22	    3: ((0.45, 0.49, 0.55, 1), 0.3, 1.0),     # metal
23	    6: ((0.10, 0.11, 0.14, 1), 0.45, 0.7),    # dark metal
24	    7: ((0.52, 0.50, 0.45, 1), 0.9, 0.0),     # plaster
25	    10: ((0.72, 0.35, 0.05, 1), 0.75, 0.0),   # hazard
26	}
27	
28	def mat_basic(name, color, rough, metal):
29	    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
30	    m.use_nodes = True
31	    b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
32	    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = color
33	    b.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = rough
34	    b.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metal
35	    return m
36	
37	def mat_neon(name, rgb):
38	    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
39	    m.use_nodes = True
40	    b = m.node_tree.nodes['Principled BSDF']
41	    mx = max(rgb) or 1
42	    col = (rgb[0] / mx, rgb[1] / mx, rgb[2] / mx, 1)
43	    b.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0, 0, 0, 1)
44	    b.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value = col
45	    b.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value = 22.0 * mx
46	    return m
47	
48	for map_id, md in DATA.items():
49	    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
50	    sc = bpy.context.scene
51	    sc.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
52	    sc.cycles.samples = 128
53	    sc.cycles.use_denoising = True
54	    sc.render.film_transparent = False
55	    sc.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
56	    sc.view_settings.look = 'High Contrast'
57	
58	    theme = md['THEME']
59	    # world: theme sky as a gradient-ish flat color (horizon tone)
60	    world = bpy.data.worlds.new('w')
61	    sc.world = world
62	    world.use_nodes = True
63	    bg = world.node_tree.nodes['Background']
64	    sh = theme['skyHorizon']
65	    bg.inputs['Color'].default_value = (sh[0], sh[1], sh[2], 1)
66	    bg.inputs['Strength'].default_value = 0.6
67	
68	    mats = {k: mat_basic(f'm{k}', *v) for k, v in MAT_LOOK.items()}
69	    mats[4] = mat_neon('neonA', theme['neonA'])
70	    mats[5] = mat_neon('neonB', theme['neonB'])
71	
72	    cx, cz = 0.0, 0.0
73	    for i, b in enumerate(md['BOXES']):
74	        x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, mid = b
75	        w, h, d = x1 - x0, y1 - y0, z1 - z0
76	        # blender: z up; game: y up -> map (x, z, y)
77	        bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=((x0 + x1) / 2, (z0 + z1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2))
78	        o = bpy.context.object
79	        o.scale = (w, d, h)
80	        bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)
81	        o.data.materials.append(mats.get(int(mid), mats[7]))
82	
83	    # theme lights (convert a handful to point lamps)
84	    for L in md['LIGHTS'][:10]:
85	        x, y, z, r, g, bch, inten = L
86	        if inten <= 0: continue
87	        bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='POINT', location=(x, z, y))
88	        lamp = bpy.context.object
89	        lamp.data.color = (r, g, bch)
90	        lamp.data.energy = inten * 60
91	        lamp.data.shadow_soft_size = 0.6
92	
93	    # sun
94	    sd = md['SUN_DIR']; scol = md['SUN_COLOR']
95	    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='SUN')
96	    sun = bpy.context.object
97	    sun.data.color = (scol[0], scol[1], scol[2])
98	    sun.data.energy = 2.2
99	    import mathutils
100	    sun.rotation_euler = mathutils.Vector((-sd[0], -sd[2], -sd[1])).to_track_quat('Z', 'Y').to_euler()
101	
102	    # isometric-ish camera: high 3/4 from south-east, frame whole arena
103	    ground = md['BOXES'][0]
104	    span = max(ground[3] - ground[0], ground[5] - ground[2])
105	    dist = span * 1.25
106	    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(dist * 0.62, -dist * 0.78, dist * 0.66))
107	    cam = bpy.context.object
108	    cam.rotation_euler = mathutils.Vector((-dist * 0.62, dist * 0.78, -dist * 0.62)).to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()
109	    cam.data.angle = math.radians(35)
110	    sc.camera = cam
111	
112	    sc.render.resolution_x = 720
113	    sc.render.resolution_y = 420
114	    sc.render.filepath = f'{OUT}/{map_id}.png'
115	    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
116	    print(f'rendered diorama {map_id}')
117	
118	print('ALL DIORAMAS DONE')

content.text:
Visual overhaul complete — **86/86 playtest checks passing**, Blender installed and in the pipeline.

**Blender (4.2 LTS, tarball install to `~/tools` after snap was denied sudo).** Two scripts in `blender/`:
- `weapons.py` models all 7 weapons as real meshes in Python (receivers, barrels, scopes, mags, grips, glowing neon stripes) and path-traces them with Cycles into transparent viewmodel sprites (1024×640) plus 3/4-angle buy-card art. Took three iterations driven by looking at the renders: washed-out materials → darker/rougher + dimmer key light; cropped framing → auto-framing from scene bounding box; floating grips/mags/knife-tip → a real Blender 4.2 gotcha where `transform_apply(scale=True)` silently also applies *location*, so every part was rotating around the world origin instead of its own center.
- `dioramas.py` rebuilds each map from the real `maps.js` geometry (exported to JSON) with theme-matched materials and emissive neons, and renders isometric Cycles hero shots — now the map picker backgrounds. They look genuinely good: full GI, colored bounce light.

**In-engine upgrades:**
- **Characters**: the featureless blobs are now humanoid rigs — head, emissive visor, torso, hips, plus capsule limbs (a new analytic primitive in the ray tracer) with a walk cycle driven by actual movement speed, for bots and remote players alike. One real shader bug found via screenshots: bots aiming at the camera made their gun capsules near-parallel to view rays, the intersector's denominator underflowed, and phantom hits painted a giant black rectangle — fixed with a denominator clamp plus NaN/Inf sanitization before the bloom chain.
- **HDR bloom**: scene now renders linear HDR to a half-float FBO; bright-pass → quarter-res separable gaussian → ACES composite. Neon strips, visors, and the foundry's ember lighting actually *glow* now. New `graphics.bloom` setting wired into all presets.
- **Viewmodels**: canvas rectangles replaced by the Cycles sprites with bob, recoil kick, inertial sway that lags camera turns, reload dip, and a star-spiked muzzle flash anchored to the actual barrel tip.
- **FX & sky**: 3D impact sparks with gravity (warm for walls, red for flesh), nebula bands and dual-density stars in the sky.

**Verification**: playtest grew to 86 checks (sprite assets serve + decode, bloom visibly changes 10% of pixels, capsule limbs exist and animate between walk phases) — two pre-existing checks had to become sim-time-based because the heavier scene drops SwiftShader to ~3 fps and wall-clock waits raced. Full visual audit screenshots in `playtest/audit/`: weapon sprites in-hand, bot squads with bloom halos, all three maps, buy menu with weapon art.
